new.s: In which state is Chandipur, where the sea recedes a few kilometres from the shore at ebb tide, located?
new.x: Chandipur on the Odisha coast is known for the sea receding a few km at low tide and coming back at high tide.
new.angle: U0613 #10 Coasts where the sea recedes far -> Chandipur

new.s: At which of the following places can one walk on the sea floor when the sea recedes several kilometres at low tide?
new.x: At Chandipur (Odisha) the sea recedes a few kilometres at ebb tide, exposing the sea floor.
new.angle: U0613 #10 Coasts where the sea recedes far -> Chandipur

new.s: What happens to the height of a tsunami wave as it enters shallow coastal water?
new.x: As the water becomes shallow the tsunami slows down and its energy piles up, so the wave height rises sharply near the coast.
new.angle: U0613 #13 Tsunami vs wind waves -> behaviour near coast (APPSC PYQ ydf8687df3ae / ycb01d873fe9)

new.s: Why does a tsunami cause little damage over the deep ocean but great damage at the coast?
o: It is weaker in deep water because winds are calmer there
Its wave height is low in deep water and rises when it slows down in shallow water
It forms only near the coast
It is stopped by ocean currents in deep water
new.x: In deep water a tsunami is fast but low; near the shore it slows down and its height builds up, so its impact is greatest at the coast.
new.angle: U0613 #13 Tsunami vs wind waves -> deep ocean vs coast (APPSC PYQ ycb01d873fe9)

new.s: In the Indian Tsunami Early Warning System, what is the role of bottom pressure recorders placed in the deep ocean?
o: They measure wind speed over the sea
They confirm that a tsunami has been generated
They record rainfall over the coast
new.x: Bottom pressure recorders on the deep sea floor sense the change in water pressure and confirm that a tsunami has been triggered.
new.angle: U0613 #9 Coastal hazard forecasting -> ITEWS sensors (APPSC PYQ y71207fe73e6)

new.s: By about how many minutes does high tide occur later each day at a place?
new.x: High tides recur about every 12 hours 25 minutes, so high tide comes about 50 minutes later each day.
new.angle: U0613 #3 Tides -> timing (notes gap)

new.s: Which of the following is a warm current of the South Pacific Ocean?
new.x: The East Australian Current is a warm current of the South Pacific; Humboldt, California and Falkland are cold currents.
new.angle: U0613 #1 Ocean currents -> warm or cold (notes gap)

new.s: Which phase of the Indian Ocean Dipole can offset the effect of El Nino on the Indian monsoon?
new.x: A positive IOD (warmer western Indian Ocean) usually strengthens the monsoon and can offset El Nino.
new.angle: U0613 #12 Indian Ocean Dipole -> monsoon link (notes gap)

new.s: Across which two oceans does the Southern Oscillation, the pressure seesaw between Tahiti and Port Darwin, operate?
new.x: The Southern Oscillation is an atmospheric pressure seesaw between the Pacific and Indian Oceans, measured as Tahiti minus Port Darwin.
new.angle: U0614 #3 ENSO -> oceans in the Southern Oscillation seesaw

new.s: What is the atmospheric pressure seesaw between Tahiti and Port Darwin called?
new.x: The pressure seesaw between Tahiti and Port Darwin is the Southern Oscillation, the atmospheric part of ENSO, first described by Gilbert Walker.
new.angle: U0614 #3 ENSO -> Southern Oscillation

new.s: In which year was El Nino linked to a monsoon deficit of about 12% below normal in India?
new.x: In 2014, El Nino conditions were linked to India's monsoon deficit of about 12% below normal.
new.angle: U0614 #1 El Nino -> impacts (APPSC PYQ y296884445b4 angle, notes gap)

new.s: Which cold current off the coast of Peru is replaced by the warm El Nino current?
new.x: During El Nino a warm current flows south along Peru and replaces the cold Humboldt (Peruvian) current.
new.angle: U0614 #1 El Nino -> current changes off Peru (notes gap)

new.s: What happens to the fish catch off the coast of Peru during El Nino?
o: It shifts to cold-water species only
new.x: El Nino stops the cold nutrient-rich upwelling off Peru, so phytoplankton fall and the fish catch collapses.
new.angle: U0614 #1 El Nino -> impacts off Peru (notes gap)

new.s: From which ocean does the eastward pulse of clouds and rain of the Madden-Julian Oscillation begin?
new.x: The MJO is an eastward pulse of clouds and rain that starts from a warm pool in the tropical Indian Ocean.
new.angle: U0614 #6 Madden-Julian Oscillation -> origin (notes gap)

new.s: What happens to coral polyps during coral bleaching?
o: They expel their zooxanthellae and turn white
They absorb extra calcium carbonate and turn red
They are covered by sea grass
They stop breathing and dissolve at once
new.x: In bleaching, stressed polyps expel the zooxanthellae algae and lose their pigments, so the coral turns white.
new.angle: U0615 #4 Coral bleaching -> symbiont expelled (APPSC PYQ y9eedd55e81f)

new.s:
Consider the following statements about coral bleaching:
1. Corals expel the zooxanthellae living in their tissues and turn white.
2. A bleached coral is always dead.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Bleaching is the expulsion of zooxanthellae, which turns coral white; bleached coral is stressed but not necessarily dead.
new.angle: U0615 #4 Coral bleaching -> symbiont expelled (APPSC PYQ y9eedd55e81f)

new.s: Which island group of India has the only true atolls in the country?
o: Islands of the Gulf of Mannar
Islands of the Gulf of Kutch
new.x: Lakshadweep is formed by coral and has India's only true atolls.
new.angle: U0615 #6 Coral reef areas -> Lakshadweep atolls (APPSC PYQ ydf096c8a6a1)

new.s: In which of the following states are true coral reefs NOT found?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh has no true reefs because of river sediment and freshwater; Tamil Nadu (Gulf of Mannar), Gujarat (Gulf of Kutch) and Maharashtra (Malvan) have reefs.
new.angle: U0615 #6 Indian regions without reefs (notes gap)

new.s: Which technology, based on mineral accretion, is used to restore damaged coral reefs?
new.x: Biorock (mineral accretion) technology is used to restore damaged coral reefs.
new.angle: U0615 #1 Coral reefs -> restoration (notes gap)

new.s: In which sea does the Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest living structure, lie?
new.x: The Great Barrier Reef lies off Queensland in the Coral Sea, part of the Pacific Ocean.
new.angle: U0615 #6 Coral reef areas -> Great Barrier Reef location (notes gap)

new.s: Which of the following is a man-made disaster?
new.x: The Bhopal gas tragedy (1984) was a chemical-industrial, man-made disaster; the others are natural hazards.
new.angle: U0616 #13 Classification -> natural vs man-made (APPSC PYQ y3380748225c)

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Droughts, heatwaves and cold waves are climatological disasters.
2. The Chernobyl accident was a natural disaster.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Droughts, heatwaves and cold waves are climatological; Chernobyl was a man-made nuclear disaster.
new.angle: U0616 #13 Classification -> natural vs man-made (APPSC PYQ y3380748225c)

new.s: Which of the following is a natural warning sign of an approaching tsunami?
o: Sudden receding of the sea from the shore
A sharp rise in air temperature
new.x: A sudden receding of the sea, a rapid rise of the sea and quake shaking are warning signs of a tsunami.
